notes: State-space search and serialization bench whose three deliverables are chained off ONE correct BFS. dependent_stages=3: the per-depth frontier files, the checksum sidecar, the depth/count summary, the parent-oriented DAG-edge CSV, and the shortest-path move trace are all arithmetic consequences of the same breadth-first pass, so a bug in traversal tees off all five artifact types at once. reasoning_depth=2: the agent must pin down breadth-first depth (distance from start), first-discovery parent semantics, ascending node-id ordering for determinism, and the parent->child orientation of the search-tree edges. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden cases include a disconnected goal (build trace must fall back to just the starter board), start==goal (single-node trace, still exploring neighbors), and a malformed graph with duplicate edges, a self-loop, and a dangling edge to an undefined node id that must be ignored. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app program is re-run on four unseen graphs and every artifact re-validated by an independent reference BFS. quantitative_correctness=2: frontier member sets, depth counts, the sha256 checksums (data must equal the re-hash of the actual bytes on disk), CSV headers and edge ordering must match exactly. Difficulty sits at the hard floor of competency C-c18fff1c (save DAG edges as a from,to CSV) and requires breadth-first reasoning plus exact serialization, not prompt length.
